issues.description: The problem statement and template define/expect an instance method named attend(course:) on Developer, but the solution implementation provides a different method name participateIn(course:). Additionally, the solution's Client calls attend(course:), which does not match the solution's Developer implementation. This name/signature mismatch is structural and will prevent the code from compiling and will confuse students about which method to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name and signature consistent across artifacts. Implement attend(course:) in Developer (extension) exactly as specified in the problem and template (or rename all references to participateIn(course:) including in Client and the problem statement). Preferably restore attend(course:) in the solution Developer.swift and ensure Client calls attend(course:) so the repository compiles and matches the exercise instructions.

issues.description: The problem statement and the template expect a Developer instance method named attend(course:), but the solution implementation defines the corresponding method as participateIn(course:). This naming mismatch breaks the direct mapping between the requirement and the provided implementation and also conflicts with the solution's Client code which calls attend(course:). Students could be confused about which method to implement and how to test it.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the solution method participateIn(course:) to attend(course:) (and update any internal references) so its name matches the problem statement and the template; alternatively, consistently rename attend(course:) to participateIn(course:) across the problem statement, template, and all call sites (e.g., Client.swift).
